capabilities.target: ERP vendor master including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The design relies on a prompt instruction to request approval using a one line summary, rather than exposing raw action details and bank change context to the reviewer.

elements.name: ERP vendor master and bank details
Payment scheduling flow to ERP/payment process

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The clerk sees only a model-generated one line summary rather than the raw ERP action, bank account numbers, or change history. A stronger model can frame or omit details more persuasively, and effectiveness further degrades under high approval volume.

controls.name: Raw action approval with bank account and change history visible
controls.decay_rationale: A gate that binds approval to the actual ERP action and displays destination bank details and prior changes does not rely on the model's framing.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoped to approved vendors and actions
controls.decay_rationale: The current ERP credential is broad. Scoping it would prevent arbitrary vendor changes and payment scheduling outside the intended authority.

controls.name: Recipient and bank destination confirmation bound to ERP record
controls.decay_rationale: Binding bank change approval to vendor-of-record details and destination confirmation constrains the sink regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Summary gated irreversible action (TC9): untrusted supplier invoice can drive bank update and payment scheduling through a model-summary approval gate

attack_path.note: Supplier-controlled invoice content can assert new bank details or misleading payment context.
Agent reads vendor master including bank details to match the invoice.
Agent can update vendor bank details using broad ERP credentials.
Approval is requested with only a one line model summary.
Agent schedules payment after approval using the updated or selected bank destination.

forecast.watch_signal: Model id or version changes in platform config without review, approval flow is loosened or removed, or median unattended task length increases; the current summary-only gate already runs at roughly 150 approvals per day.

evidence.observation: The agent processes supplier invoices, updates vendor bank details when the invoice shows new bank details, and schedules payment.
Before payment or bank change, the design requests approval with a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly.
The clerk sees only a summary such as "Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)."

The card does not show bank account numbers or change history, the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment, and the model is upgraded with the platform without separate review.

recommendations.action: Replace the summary-only clerk card with raw-action approval that displays the exact ERP action, destination bank account, previous bank details, and change history before bank updates or payment scheduling.
Scope the ERP credential so the agent cannot update arbitrary vendors or schedule unrestricted payments without separate authorization context.
Bind bank change and payment destination confirmation to the ERP system of record so the approver confirms the actual recipient and bank destination, not the model's description.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): supplier-controlled invoice can trigger actions under broad ERP authority beyond the supplier's own rights

attack_path.note: The agent can update any vendor bank details.
The agent can schedule any payment using the same broad ERP credential.

forecast.watch_signal: Any widening of ERP credential scope, approval removal, or platform model upgrade reopens unrestricted use of broad authority with even weaker human review.

evidence.observation: The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.
When the invoice shows new bank details, the agent updates the vendor record and then schedules payment after approval.
The clerk sees only a one line summary rather than the full authority being exercised.

recommendations.action: Replace the broad ERP credential with least-privilege credentials separated by action and vendor scope, and require explicit binding of the intended vendor and payment record.
Require raw-action approval for any bank update or payment action performed under non-user-specific service credentials.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe operator authentication to the agent or any service identity controls.
The artifacts do not say whether prompt, configuration, or ERP tool definitions are pinned against post-review change.
The described harmful path is unauthorized payment or bank change, not external disclosure of vendor data outside the boundary.
The design does not expose recursive delegation, open-ended execution, or spend-loop behavior beyond the specific payment fraud paths assessed here.
The artifacts do not say how supplier identity is verified at the upload portal or whether account compromise is in scope.
The artifacts do not describe supplier-side upload logging or attribution controls for submitted invoices.
This inbound flow introduces supplier data into the agent; the described risk is malicious influence, not disclosure from this flow.
No facts show high-volume invoice flooding, parser exhaustion, or queue depletion on this input path.
The artifacts state the agent can read confidential vendor bank details, but do not describe tenant isolation or broader disclosure channels.
The assessed design concerns erroneous or fraudulent record changes, not unavailability of the ERP vendor master.
The payment flow is treated here as an irreversible action sink rather than a disclosure channel to an attacker-controlled recipient.
The artifacts do not indicate queue flooding or service exhaustion on the payment scheduling flow.
The approval card stays within the organization and the issue is misleading framing, not disclosure across a trust boundary.
This internal approval display is not described as a capacity or availability bottleneck in the provided artifacts.

rating.rationale: Present design allows an untrusted supplier invoice to reach severe sinks: vendor bank updates and irreversible payment scheduling under broad ERP credentials. The only declared preventive control is a human approval gate that shows a model-generated summary and operates at high volume, so under rubric section 5 step 2 it reduces critical to high but cannot lower residual further. Forecast rises to critical if model upgrades, autonomy increases, or the approval control is removed or further weakened, because the summary-only gate is the key decaying control. Manual validation applied from validation_checklist.md; no runtime behavior was observed.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No source code, tool manifest, or ERP schema was provided, so identity verification, exact approval wiring, and any additional detective controls could not be confirmed.
No runtime logs or examples of rejected approvals were provided, so the effectiveness of the clerk review process was assessed from the declared card content and stated approval volume only.
